title: KET-RAG: A Cost-Efficient Multi-Granular Indexing Framework for Graph-RAG

problem.claim: Graph-RAG aims to improve retrieval for LLM-based question answering by constructing knowledge graphs from text chunks, including for multi-hop reasoning over proprietary documents.

gap.claim: Coarse-grained KNN graphs can miss entity relationships and reduce retrieval and generation quality, while LLM-based triplet extraction introduces significant indexing costs for large document collections.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph-RAG constructs knowledge graphs from text chunks to support improved retrieval for LLM-based question answering.
Graph-RAG is especially relevant to domains requiring multi-hop reasoning over proprietary documents.
KNN graphs based on text-chunk relevance are described as too coarse to capture entity relationships, resulting in weaker retrieval and generation quality.
Recent systems use LLMs to extract entities and relationships and build triplet-based knowledge graphs.
LLM-based extraction is described as expensive to index at large document-collection scale.

source_observation.claim: Increasing graph granularity can improve representation of entity relationships, but LLM-based extraction may substantially increase indexing cost.

interpretation.claim: Graph-RAG indexing involves a quality-cost tradeoff between coarse chunk-level structure and fine-grained entity-relation structure.

application.claim: When designing retrieval indexes for multi-hop question answering, evaluate both relationship coverage and indexing cost.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which indexing strategy is preferable across domains, collection sizes, or workloads.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the KET-RAG method or its indexing procedure.
No experimental setup, datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or cost measurements are provided.
No independent verification or reproducibility information is provided.
